Question Choices: A square is divided into 6 equal parts, and 4 parts are coloured green. What fraction of the square is green?
Hints: Fraction is displayed by shaded parts (numerator) / total equal parts (denominator). Count how many parts are green. Count how many parts the whole square has.
Solution: Four of the 6 equal parts are green, so the fraction is 4/6.

Question Choices: A cake has 8 slices, all the same size. What is the fraction of 1 slice?
Hints: Fractions show 1 part out of the whole. The denominator tells how many equal pieces the whole cake is cut into.
Solution: One of 8 equal slices is 1/8 of the cake.

Question Choices: Select. A triangle is divided into 3 parts, but one part is smaller. Can this show thirds (1/3)? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: To show fractions, the whole must be divided into equal parts. If one part is smaller, does it still count as equal?
Solution: No. Thirds must be three equal parts. A smaller part means these parts are not thirds.

Question Choices: A chocolate bar is cut into 8 equal pieces. If 3 pieces have almonds, what fraction has almonds?
Hints: Identify the total number of equal pieces (denominator). Identify how many pieces have almonds (numerator). Then write a fraction: almond pieces / total pieces
Solution: Three of the 8 equal pieces contain almonds. The fraction is 3/8.

Question Choices: Select. A rectangle is cut into 2 equal and 1 small extra piece. Can we say the larger pieces are 2/3? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: To show fractions, the whole must be divided into equal parts. If one part is smaller, does it still count as equal?
Solution: No. The three pieces are unequal. Each larger piece is more than 1/3, so the two larger pieces together are more than 2/3 of the rectangle.
